role: Trends-tab monthly calendar (Sun-Sat grid) of the user's sessions showing per-day training LOAD, morning-feeling dot, weekly and monthly totals, month navigation, plus a private day-summary sheet that lists the day's sessions and lets the user soft-delete one via the parent's onDelete closure.

HistoryCalendarView.DayCell: private struct — one grid cell (date, in-month flag, summed load, sessions, overnight morningFeeling)
HistoryCalendarView.WeekRow: private struct — 7 DayCells + in-month weekly load
HistoryCalendarView.MonthStats: private struct — month total load + session count
DaySheetIdentity: private struct (Identifiable, id = date) — sheet item
DaySummarySheet: private struct (View, @MainActor) — per-day session list with delete via context menu + confirmation
state: mem:HistoryCalendarView.visibleMonth (@State, start of current month at creation)
toplevel: onDelete defaults to `{ _ in false }` (line 30), so a caller that omits it gets a sheet whose every delete shows the failure alert. visibleMonth initialised to startOfMonth(Date()) (line 32). memoizedMonthStats initial MonthStats(0,0). DaySheetIdentity.id is the date so the sheet identity ignores session content. Only callers: TrendsV2View.swift:218 (onDelete: deleteSession) and EmuquTests/ScreenSnapshotTests.swift:35,46.

flags.text: Days are bucketed by cal.startOfDay(session.startDate) (lines 437-440), so an overnight that starts before midnight (e.g. Mon 23:00) lands on Monday's cell together with its morning-feeling dot, while the History list (HistoryView via SessionArchiveEntry.displayDate = sleepEnd/endDate for overnights) shows the same night under Tuesday; month totals (line 421-423) also attribute a Sep-30-23:00 night to September. The doc comment at 397-399 calls it the overnight that 'anchors' the day, but the anchor is bedtime, not the wake day the feeling was rated on.

Header doc lists the load resolver as powerTSS → hrTSS → METs → luciaTRIMP → route-history, but WorkoutMetadata.preferredTrainingLoad puts route-history (extrapolatedTRIMP) second when routeEstimateReplacesHRLoad is true.

ARCHITECTURE.md says nights are keyed by the wake date (SleepSchedule.nightKey); the calendar keys every session, overnights included, by cal.startOfDay(startDate), so a night begun before midnight and its morning-feeling dot sit on the previous day.
